title: Don’t let cyber foes haunt you this October

body_markdown:
Ghosts, goblins, and things that go bump in the night aren’t the only scary threats lurking this time of year.


While Halloween is full of spooky surprises, Cybersecurity Awareness Month serves as an important reminder that some of today’s most dangerous threats exist online. Cybercriminals are becoming faster, smarter, and more convincing than ever, aided by the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to power new scams and attacks. The good news? You don’t need a silver bullet or magic spell to protect yourself.


This year’s Cybersecurity Awareness Month theme, “Don’t Make It Easy For Them,” encourages all of us to build simple, consistent habits that make life much more difficult for cybercriminals. The National Cybersecurity Alliance[recommends](https://www.staysafeonline.org/cybersecurity-awareness-month) four key actions—use strong, unique, passwords with a password manager; turn on multifactor authentication (MFA); recognize and report scams; and keep your software updated.


Let’s look at some of the cyber threats that may be lurking in your online realm:


**The Phantom Phisher**


Imagine opening an email that appears to be from your bank, favorite retailer, or even a friend. Everything seems normal, but it’s actually a trap designed to steal your personal information.


Phishing scams remain one of the most common ways cybercriminals gain access to passwords, financial information, and online accounts. These messages often create a sense of urgency, hoping you’ll act quickly.


Treat suspicious emails, texts, and messages like a haunted house—if something feels off, don’t go inside and risk it. Verify requests through a trusted source before clicking links or downloading attachments.


**The AI** **Doppelgänger**


One of the newest monsters on the block is powered by artificial intelligence.


AI allows criminals to create more convincing phishing emails, fake websites, realistic images, and even cloned voices. Cybercriminals can use AI tools to generate personalized scams in seconds, making fraudulent messages harder to spot than ever before. The Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)[warns](https://www.cisa.gov/cybersecurity-awareness-month) that AI is accelerating the rate at which attackers can identify vulnerabilities and target victims.


When something seems unusual, pause and verify before responding. In the age of AI, skepticism is becoming one of the best cybersecurity tools available.


**The Invisible Account Thief**


Even strong passwords can sometimes fall into the wrong hands. That’s why unique passwords and MFA are so important. Utilizing a password manager makes keeping track of all your passwords easy and secure.


MFA adds a second layer of protection by requiring an additional verification step, such as a code sent to your phone or generated by an authentication app. Even if a criminal steals your password, MFA can stop them from gaining access to your account. Think of MFA as the deadbolt on your digital front door.
